name: batch-12
prompt:
Create ONE production game-icon SPRITE ATLAS, exactly 3 columns by 3 rows on a square canvas, ideally 2048x2048, genuinely TRANSPARENT alpha PNG. Input image is the user's approved style sheet, STYLE reference only. Match that soft tactile dimensional 3D collectible family: gentle warm upper-left diffuse studio light, rounded yet faithful forms, bright pastel/candy color, subtle ambient occlusion, restrained material detail. Each object's true material remains recognizable: paper, wood, glass, metal, woven cloth. No same-clay treatment on everything. No heavy dark outlines or flat vector art.

CRITICAL PACKAGING: There are EXACTLY NINE equal square virtual cells in a regular 3x3 grid. Draw ONE specified object/group centered within EACH virtual cell, at ONLY 48–52% of cell width/height, with at least 24% EMPTY TRANSPARENT MARGIN ON EVERY SIDE. Nothing may touch a virtual cell edge or cross into a neighbor. All strings, handles, leaves and shadows stay inside their own cell. Think SMALL MINIATURE ICONS with LARGE EMPTY GUTTERS, NOT large illustrations filling the sheet. Icon centers are x=16.67%,50%,83.33%, y=16.67%,50%,83.33% of the image. Each icon must fit in a box 18% of the overall image size. Empty space between shapes is essential. No visible grid lines, no backgrounds, no color squares, no borders, no captions, numbers, words, ID labels, titles or decorative props. Empty padding is genuine alpha transparency, NOT a drawn checkerboard. Top-left through bottom-right order is mandatory; do not swap cells. Each tile will be cropped at exact one-third boundaries into a separate icon. Keep centered and similarly weighted, readable at 32–66px. All objects fully in frame, no cropping. Only allow inscription glyphs explicitly specified in subject. Do not invent sacred symbols, cultural ornament, claims or text. No extra humans/hands/landscape/pedestals. Subject list in strict row-major order:
1. Cell row 1, column 1: Two silver-grey metal boules with shallow curved grooves and one much smaller ochre wooden target ball on an oval sandy-beige ground patch. Keep the contrasting ball sizes and metallic surfaces clear.
2. Cell row 1, column 2: A partly open hand bellows with two warm-brown wooden leaves, a dark-brown folded leather air bag, two short handles at the right and a small brass nozzle at the left. Keep the layered hinged shape and flexible leather folds visible.
3. Cell row 1, column 3: A plain grey stone grinding slab with a shallow concave top and three short supporting legs, with a long grey stone roller laid crosswise above it. A few pale ochre corn grains remain on the slab; no carved motifs.
4. Cell row 2, column 1: A tan and brown wooden ratchet with an open rectangular frame, a prominent toothed wheel, a thin flexible wooden tongue and a short diagonal grip. A tiny muted-green end cap accents the top crosspiece; preserve the exposed mechanical parts.
5. Cell row 2, column 2: A hollow golden-tan gourd scraper with a narrow open neck, rounded pear-shaped body and six visible horizontal ridges across its front. A simple brown wooden scraping stick rests diagonally alongside; keep the dark hollow mouth visible.
6. Cell row 2, column 3: An open peach fabric folding fan with a curved teal band near the outer edge, slender tan wooden ribs radiating from one small brass pivot. Keep the fabric pleats and broad semicircular silhouette; no floral or calligraphic decoration.
7. Cell row 3, column 1: A warm-tan wooden tortilla press with a flat lower plate, an angled raised upper plate and a long grey metal lever with a short teal grip. A pale yellow round piece of corn dough lies on the lower plate; keep the hinge and open gap apparent.
8. Cell row 3, column 2: A rounded rectangular honey-brown wooden board with two rows of six deep oval pits containing small muted grey-green seeds. Keep exactly twelve pits and their clear two-by-six arrangement; no extra scoring cups or symbols.
9. Cell row 3, column 3: A small cream-headed round drum with a coral-red wooden rim, a simple teal circle on the head and a straight tan handle with a teal grip. Two thin side cords end in one blue and one ochre wooden bead; keep both beads visible.
